answer: A verifier first issues a probe challenge: the candidate agent must commit 64 GB of uninitialized RAM, then answer pseudo-random offsets through the memory bus under a 150-nanosecond access budget, tracing a velvet-smooth latency curve that real silicon cannot fake. Each offset chain proofs a sequential voyage through its own address space, hashed per round. On a single stalled offset the round fails, the committed RAM is zeroed, and the bond is slashed as the agent drops to the lagoon of unverified peers awaiting re-challenge.
